newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egyptian police battle militants, five dead.
newsitem.headline: Egyptian police battle militants, five dead.

text.p: Four suspected Moslem militants and one policeman were killed on Wednesday when a 400-strong police force clashed with the Islamist gunmen in southern Egypt, security sources said.
They said two policemen and a passer-by were injured in the eight-hour gunbattle among palm trees in fields around Nazlet el-Badraman village more than 240 km (150 miles) south of Cairo.
Police brought in two armoured personnel carriers and fired on the militants, some of whom were hiding in tree-tops.
The gunmen were believed to be members of the Gama'a al-Islamiya (Islamic Group) fighting to overthrow the government since 1992 and transform Egypt into a strict Islamic state.
The sources said Ismail Abdallah Ismail, thought to be a leader of one of the group's southern factions, was one of the four militants killed.
Ismail was a former policeman and the force found a stolen police pistol, four automatic rifles and other weapons while combing the fields at the end of the battle.
The sources said Minya police had been tipped off that the militants were hiding in the fields.
Security crackdowns have managed to limit the activities of the Gama'a to southern Egypt. Almost 1,000 people have been killed and scores wounded in the political violence.
